summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of COPD, chronic DVT/PE, atrial myxoma, and chronic pain was admitted for bilateral lower extremity swelling and dyspnea. He had worsening right leg swelling two days prior, followed by left leg involvement, and reported shortness of breath with ambulation and cough. Initial workup ruled out pulmonary embolism and infection. Elevated BNP and clinical findings suggested new-onset heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. Edema improved with IV diuresis, and dyspnea resolved with bronchodilators and optimized COPD management. High sodium intake from V8 juice and recent high-dose prednisone were identified as contributing factors. The patient remained hemodynamically stable, with improved symptoms and near-resolution of edema at discharge. Social work addressed homelessness, though the patient declined shelter referrals. A follow-up appointment was arranged, and he was discharged home with a plan to continue anticoagulation, diuresis, and respiratory medications.
problems: Hypertensive heart disease with heart failure
Personal history of other venous thrombosis and embolism
Family history of ischemic heart disease and other diseases of the circulatory system
